newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Law recognising poll wins likely today-Serbia pm.
newsitem.headline: Law recognising poll wins likely today-Serbia pm.

text.p: Serbian Prime Minister Mirko Marjanovic said a draft law reinstating last November's disputed local election results will probably be submitted to parliament later on Wednesday, Belgrade state radio said.
Serbia's opposition has mounted 78 days of relentless rallies demanding that their municipal election wins in 14 towns and cities, including the capital, be reinstated.
Moments after the radio report, the official Yugoslav news agency Tanjug said the Serbian government had drafted the law and was in the process of forwarding it to parliament.
On Tuesday, the autocratic Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic suddenly announced that he would ask parliament to reinstate the disputed results.
Two days earlier, Milosevic sent in his paramilitary police to break up relentless opposition protests. Repeated baton charges injured scores of people and prompted an international outcry.
The three-party opposition alliance also wants free media and an independent judiciary ahead of presidential and parliamentary elections due by the end of this year.
